content_voiceover: This slide highlights two recent phase three trials, both published in the Lancet in January 2026, evaluating novel agents added to lenalidomide and rituximab for relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma. On the left, the EPCORE FL-1 trial compared epcoritamab, a CD20 by CD3 bispecific antibody, plus lenalidomide and rituximab, against lenalidomide and rituximab alone. Progression-free survival was dramatically improved in the epcoritamab arm, with the median not yet reached compared to eleven point seven months in the control arm, a hazard ratio of zero point two one. On the right, the inMIND trial tested tafasitamab, an anti-CD19 monoclonal antibody, added to lenalidomide and rituximab, against placebo plus lenalidomide and rituximab. Median progression-free survival was twenty-two point four months with tafasitamab versus thirteen point nine months with placebo, a hazard ratio of zero point four three. Both trials demonstrate that adding a novel targeted agent, whether a bispecific antibody or an anti-CD19 antibody, to lenalidomide-rituximab substantially improves outcomes in relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma, reflecting the rapidly evolving treatment landscape fellows should be aware of for boards.

keypoint_voiceover: Two new phase three trials show major PFS benefit when adding novel agents to lenalidomide-rituximab in relapsed refractory follicular lymphoma. Epcoritamab, a bispecific antibody, in EPCORE FL-1 gave a hazard ratio of zero point two one. Tafasitamab, an anti-CD19 antibody, in inMIND gave a hazard ratio of zero point four three. Both represent important additions to the relapsed refractory treatment armamentarium.
